overview.body:
**Wamani** ​(*wamani*) ‌— ‌Sacred Mountain ​· ​The ​falcon ​— ​belongs to ‌the ​Incan ​tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌catalogued ​under ‌the ​domain ​"Sacred Mountain". ​The ​name ​means ‌"The ​falcon".

**Wamani** ‌is ​sacred ‌mountain. ​The ‌name means ​"The ‌falcon" ​and ​belongs ‌to ‌the incan ‌tradition.

​PuniCodex ​restores ‌the ​name as ​**Wamani** ‌and ​serves ​its ‌temple at ​[its ‌temple](https://punicodex.com/wamani/). ​The ​restoration ​needs no ​distinctive ‌letters ‌or ​diacritics ‌its ASCII ​form ​would ‌lose, ‌which ‌places ‌the name ​in ‌Tier ​2. ​The ​plain ASCII ‌form ​*wamani* ​survives ​as ‌a modern ​convenience ​imposed ​by ‌the ​early domain-name ‌system; ​the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the fallback, ‌is ​the ​form ​the ​project defends ‌as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation ‌survives for ​this ​name; ​**Wamani** is ​a ​scholarly transliteration ‌of ​the reconstructed ​spoken ‌form. ​Etymologically the ‌name ​means "The ‌falcon".

​The ASCII ​form ​*wamani* ​survives only ​because ‌the early ​domain-name ‌system could ​not ‌carry ​diacritics; it ‌is ​a technological ‌compromise, ​not an ​ancient ‌spelling. ‌The Unicode ‌restoration ​**Wamani** recovers ​the ‌full diacritic ​detail ​of ‌the scholarly ​transliteration ​directly in ‌the ​address bar. ‌The ​restoration needs ​no ​distinctive ​letters or ‌diacritics ‌its ASCII ​form ‌would lose, ​which ​places ‌the name ‌in ‌Tier 2.

‌The ​letter-by-letter transformation ‌runs:

​- ​**w** → ​**W** ‌— Same, ​capitalized
​- **a** ​→ ‌**a** ​— Same
​- ​**m** → ‌**m** ​— Same
‌- ​**a** ‌→ **a** ​— ‌Same
- ‌**n** ​→ **n** ​— ​Same
​- **i** ‌→ ‌**i** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/wamani/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**wamani** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Wamani.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"wamani" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Wamani".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"wamani" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Wamani" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Wamani was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Wamani ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Wamani ‌place ​sacred mountain ​at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living ​mythological world.

​### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Wamani ‌appears ​in incan ‌tradition ​as ​sacred mountain. ​The ​name's ​meaning, "The ‌falcon", ​shapes the ‌narratives ​told ‌about this ​figure.

‌### ​Worship and ‌Memory ​(Cult)

​Devotees and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ‌Wamani ​in ​ritual, text, ‌and ​iconography, ​ensuring the ‌name ​survived ​into the ‌modern ​scholarly record.

‌The ​myths ​of Wamani ​survive ​in ‌fragments, summaries, ‌and ​later ‌retellings. Each ​version ​reflects the ‌interests ‌of ‌its tellers ‌— ​poets, ‌priests, philosophers, ​and ​scholars. ​The PuniCodex ‌entry ​does not ​privilege ​a ‌single version; ​it ​gathers ​the attestations ‌so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. The ​restoration ‌Wamani ‌gives the ​figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or artifact ​in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet assigned ​to ‌Wamani ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should be ​read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Incan ​name ‌of this ​type ‌the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected to ​be ​thin, ‌and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains the ‌textual ​testimony ​gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources section.

​Were ‌such ​evidence ​to ​surface, ​it ‌would take ‌recognizable ​forms: ‌votive ​or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming Wamani, ‌sanctuary ‌or ​cult ‌remains ​tied ​to sacred ​mountain ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional ​attributes (name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be ‌weighed against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name ​before entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Wamani ‌is to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of ​sacred Mountain ‌in ​the ​mind ‌and ​to ask ‌what ​of ‌it ​endures. ​The name ​means ​"The ​falcon" ‌— ​and a ‌name ​that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning so ​openly ‌invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere recollection. ‌The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​sacred ‌Mountain ​· ​The ‌falcon.

Sit ​with ‌the ​restored ​form ​— Wamani ​— ‌and ‌the ​diacritics ‌themselves become ​the ​practice: ‌each ‌mark ‌is ‌a small ​act ‌of ​attention, ​a ​refusal to ‌let ​the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form *wamani* ​stand ​in ​for ‌the ​whole. What ‌the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this name, ‌the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader to ‌preserve ‌in ​turn.
